newsitem.title: UK: Asda Property shares drop as MD quits.
newsitem.headline: Asda Property shares drop as MD quits.

text.p: Shares in Asda Property Holdings Plc tumbled on Thursday after the company said its managing director Tony Roscoe was to quit because of differences with the rest of the company's board.
The stock was down 21p at 148 by 1046 GMT in volume of 140,650 shares.

The announcement came as Asda Property posted results for 1996, showing a ten percent rise in net assets per share to 143p and an eight percent rise in underlying earnings per share to 4.1p. The dividend was raised eight percent to 2.8p.

In a statement, Roscoe said: "After it became apparent that I differed from the majority of the board on a number of management isseus I felt that it was best that I leave, but I do so with some regret."
He said he had offered colleagues "full support in arranging an orderly handover" and had offered to be available in a consulting capacity as necessary.

Asda gave no further reason for the departure. Finance director Paul Huberman told Reuters the company's policy was to make no comment on the nature of Roscoe's differences with the rest of the company's board.
Roscoe had been managing director since 1991, having joined the company in 1983.
In a statement after the results, chairman Manny Davidson said the current year had started well.

"It is undoubtedly harder again in 1997 to acquire the quality of asset that we seek," Davidson said, "but on the positive side, improving investor sentiment should mean that we reap future benefit from the changes that we have made to the portfolio in recent years."
